full_judgment: 21. The defendant claimed that after execution of the sale deed, she was given possession and that the plaintiff dispossessed her after liberation of Bangladesh in 1972. The trial Court without consideration of these documents Exhibits F and F(2) held that the plaintiff is in possession of the suit property. Exhibits F and F(2) sufficiently proved that till the delivery of judgment in Title Appeal No. 391 of 1970 on 10th February, 1971, Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun being purchaser from Samir Kumar Chowdhury was in possession in a portion of the suit property. The trial Court on a misreading of Exhibit E(4) held that Samir Kumar Chowdhury admitted the possession of Md Ishaque Miah in the High Court in Writ Petition No. 99 of 1966. After the delivery of the judgment in Writ Petition No. 99 of 1966 on 9th February, 1967, the property was handed over possession to Md Ishaque Miah and Samir Kumar Chowdhury as evident from (Exhibit F) and therefore, the learned Subordinate Judge on misreading (Exhibit E( 4) and non-consideration of Exhibit F held that the plaintiff was in possession of the suit property. Over and above, since the suit for declaration of title and recovery of khas possession was instituted on 1 st October, 1977 within 12 years of the date of dispossession, the defendant Syeda Sirajunnessa Khatun having acquired title in the suit property on the strength of Exhibit G is entitled to get recovery of khas possession. The Court of appeal below, in the premises, has committed no error of law in interfering with the judgment of the trial Court and decreeing Title Suit No. 93 of 1982 arising out of Title Suit No. 157 of 1977 and dismissing Title Suit No. 68 of 1983 arising out of Title Suit No. 31 of 1970. I find no infirmity or any misreading or any non-consideration of the evidence on record by the Court of appeal below in reversing the judgment of the trial Court. On the other hand, I find that the trial Court on a superficial consideration of the evidence on record and also on misreading and non-consideration of the materials on record has decreed the suit for Specific Performance of Contract. In view of the above, I find no merit in these Rules.
